content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"title\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"revisionId\": \"1b0d9b5d65\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:00:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:41:00Z\", \"text\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "title": "Q4 investor update - send list", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list", "revisionId": "1b0d9b5d65", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:41:00Z", "text": "Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.
"}

TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.\\n\\nLeonard and team,\\n\\nThanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It\\u2019s obvious this isn\\u2019t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you\\u2019ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.\\n\\nAfter reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we\\u2019ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it\\u2019s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:\\n\\nThere\\u2019s a lot to like about what you\\u2019re building:\\n\\u2022 You\\u2019ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you\\u2019re building toward true scalability.\\n\\u2022 There\\u2019s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2\\u20133 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t\\u2019s clear you\\u2019re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.\\nWhat\\u2019s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We\\u2019d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.\\n\\nWe also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it\\u2019s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We\\u2019d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.\\n\\n\\nThis was a tough call. You\\u2019re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We\\u2019ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we\\u2019d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.\\n\\nThanks again for sharing the journey with us. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Most major ad networks, including Google AdMob, Meta Audience Network, and Unity Ads, have strict policies against *incentivized ad views* and artificial engagement.
*Potential Policy Violations*
Here’s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:
1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*
    ◦ Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it’s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).
    ◦ Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.
2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*
    ◦ Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.
    ◦ Clicks, impressions, and video views *must be organic*—forcing or incentivizing views creates *low-value interactions*, which networks can penalize.
3. *Revenue Share / Arbitrage Concerns*
    ◦ If you’re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*—where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.
    ◦ Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.
4. *Bot & Fraud Detection Risks*
    ◦ Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.
    ◦ Even if users are real, networks might still mark their engagement as *low-quality traffic* and *suspend payments*.
*Workarounds (If You Still Want Something Similar)*
If you still want a reward-based system, consider these alternatives:
1. *Use a Legitimate Rewarded Ad Model*
    ◦ AdMob, Unity, and other networks allow *rewarded ads* as long as the rewards stay within the app (e.g., coins, extra lives).
    ◦ You could design a game where *watching ads enhances gameplay* rather than directly giving real-world cash.
2. *Partner with Alternative Ad Networks*
    ◦ Some alternative ad networks (like Mistplay or OfferToro) specialize in *reward-based advertising*, but they typically *don’t allow direct ad revenue sharing*.
    ◦ Look into *GPT (Get Paid To) networks* that allow users to complete offers, surveys, and ad views for rewards *without violating policies*.
3. *Use Affiliate or Direct Sponsorships Instead*
    ◦ Instead of using standard ad networks, you could *partner with brands directly* and give users a cut of *affiliate revenue* (e.g., watching sponsored videos, completing brand challenges).
*Bottom Line*
Your current idea *will likely violate policies* and could get you *banned from major ad networks*. import re
t=open('/tmp/mail/all.txt').read()
msgs=t.split('='*100)
out=[]
seen=set()
for m in msgs:
    idl=re.search(r'ID: (.*)',m)
    if not idl: continue
    if idl.group(1) in seen: continue
    seen.add(idl.group(1))
    lines=[l for l in m.split('\n') if not l.startswith('>')]
    s='\n'.join(lines)
    # cut at "On ... wrote:"
    s=re.split(r'\nOn [^\n]{5,120}wrote:',s)[0]
    s=re.sub(r'\n\s*\n+','\n',s)
    out.append(s)
# sort by date
import email.utils
def dt(s):
    m=re.search(r'Date: (.*)',s)
    try: return email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime(m.group(1)).timestamp()
    except: return 0
out.sort(key=dt)
open('/tmp/mail/clean.txt','w').write(('\n'+'#'*80+'\n').join(out))
print(len(out))
EOF

1586	   mini-games before core is Proven

1589	   -

1591	*Do's*

1593	   Invest in the tile/level engine; create puzzles algorithmically to scale
1594	   core co[USERNAME_6805].

Hi PERSON_2574_NAME,
Thanks again for the time and the sharp questions earlier this week - we
found the discussion genuinely useful. We were a bit underprepared to
summarize our takeaways from Domino Delights on the call, so I’m sending a
clearer follow-up below and highlighting a few points that I wanted to get
across.
*Why we’re excited about LVP*
We know this market is hard. We’re looking for a lead who believes an
*engine-first &
multiple-shots at goal approach* can unlock scale; we simply didn’t raise
enough last time to fully lean into it. We also know you guys are awesome
and can really support us in our journey beyond capital injection.
*Try the current build*
We pushed an update yesterday (levels *100 → 200* plus major technical
fixes) and are gearing up for *beta-2 build*. We have 3 major features and
some polish shipping next Friday and will follow up with hopefully some
exciting KPIs, especially around playtime.
   -
   iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
   -
   Android:
   https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US
*Partnerships & roadmap*
We’re leaning into publisher/partnerships to expand capability. Next week
we have an engine deep-dive with a potential partner and will draft a
3-year engine roadmap - what [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine looks like with 10+ engineers,
Unity plugins/SDK, and a platform that operates as a growth machine. We’ll
share those notes with you to inform your process.
*Domino Delights Learnings*
*Don'ts*
   -
   Ship innovations that conflict with the game’s natural audience or theme.
   -
   Over-commit to features with unproven incremental value (e.g., saga map,
   heavy hero animations).
   -
   Build without a strong core-game engagement loop. (This is key and why
   we moved on to Zombie Match 3D)
   -
   Over-iterate on supporting mechanics (mini-games) at the expense of the
   core. - we lost too much time for unproven mini-games and mini-games act
   more like a multiplier to engagement rather than additive so don't do
   mini-games before core is Proven
   -
   Create mismatches between hero progression design and scoring mechanics.
   -
   Interrupt new players with long, text-heavy tutorials.
*Do's*
   -
   Invest in the tile/level engine; create puzzles algorithmically to scale
   core co[USERNAME_6805].
   -
   Build *reusable* LiveOps features and tools that complement the core
   game.
   -
   Stick with Proven core mechanics; apply small, audience-aware tweaks -
   especially for change-resistant segments.
   -
   Choose an art style aligned with the target audience’s preferences.
   -
   Introduce new mechanics gradually if the audience is change-resistant.
   -
   Communicate core mechanics visually and clearly.
Thanks again, and we’d love to continue the conversation if There is
interest. We’re hungry to prove this - chips on our shoulders, and the
experience to first survive, then thrive.
Best,
Leonard

*First, *a quick blurb on [SOURCE_ORG_0001].
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] is an AI-first mobile studio building the next breakout in
Puzzle RPGs. Founded in 2023, we raised a $3M seed led by [PERSON_NAME_2000] and has
grown into a 17-person distributed team. Our edge is the [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine -
an AI production platform that transforms prototypes into scalable live
games, powering level generation, adaptive difficulty, LiveOps scheduling,
and economy tuning. Version 1 is live and Proven, enabling us to ship new
titles in ~4 months with liveops fully integrated once core game is Proven.

*Domino Delights *iOS:

Android:

title because we believe it doesn’t have the $100M+ core engagement
potential without 6-12 months of investment and iteration to be a

engine’s content pipeline, physics, boosters, event systems, storefront,

day-0 playtime, ~$4.50 CPI (small sample size on Unity campaigns)
• Next 4–6 weeks: expand live events integration & 500+ levels, complete
polish/VFX, and scale tests to 2–3k users for stable reads
• Gates to proceed: ≥45% D1, ≥45% D7/D1, ≤$3.50 CPI in UK iOS. We scale
only if the data clears these bars.
Looking forward to our conversation! Let us know if you have any questions.
Best,
Leonard

2160	Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],
2161	Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
2162	core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
2163	can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
2164	that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
2165	that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
2166	both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
2167	we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
2168	difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
2169	click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
2170	make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
2171	pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
2172	we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
2173	upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
2174	battlefield.
2175	In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
2176	lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
2177	1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
2178	at zombies to strategize
2179	2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
2180	match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
2181	fire so players can tap without watching the board
2182	3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).
2183	We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
2184	for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
2185	on our end.
2186	Best,
2187	Leonard

Subject: Re: Intro: Danny, Michael (SciPlay) <> Leonard ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],
Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.
In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).
We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.
Best,
Leonard

By the way, we spoke with the Metaplay team yesterday to get a sense of engine competition. Their backend solution is very robust. They offer all the basic stuff we are offering today like leaderboards, event and inventory management, customer support plus some more around player/guild specific controls and discovery tools.
Their strategic decision of keeping their engine game-agnostic means they haven’t built feature-specific client-side libraries. It’s a strong server-side data management tool, but we believe a studio like ours can do better by reducing dev cycles with a client-side library of drag-and-drop events across casual titles. We surely can afford to be more specific since our goal together would be building a billion dolllar casual mobile studio, rather than building any genre on mobile.
Looking forward to your thoughts.
Best,
Leonard

Leonard and team,
Thanks again for walking us through [SOURCE_ORG_0001]. We really appreciated
the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your
long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were
impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating
cadence, and the product roadmap.
After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the
difficult decision not to include [SOURCE_ORG_0001] in the upcoming speedrun cohort.
In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted
to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:
There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
   - You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301],
   Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency
   that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have
   worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear
   rhythm to how you’re executing.
   - We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs
   with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a
   hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The
   fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the
   first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that
   you’re building toward true scalability.
   - There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+
   minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are
   meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new
   design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing
   you in the right direction.
What's holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and
financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4
months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it
feels a little early for us to step in. We'd want to see the new game
stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention)
before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but
still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you
to a place where you can raise the next round.
We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your
internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell
whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits,
or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We'd
love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system
matures.
------------------------------
This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team
operating with speed and discipline.

I wanted to check in and see where things stand on your side. We spoke with the Metaplay team today to get a sense of engine competition. Their backend solution is robust, but by keeping it game-agnostic they haven’t built feature-specific libraries. It’s a strong server-side data management tool, but we believe a studio like ours can go one better by reducing dev cycles with a client-side library of drag-and-drop events across casual titles. We can afford to be more specific, while the cost of acquiring someone like Metaplay would be far higher.
On our end, conversations with other VCs and companies are moving along, but nothing is concrete yet. Given the limited time left in the year, it would be good to know where your head is at and what next steps could look like. We need clarity soon in order to make sure the company can float into the new year.
Looking forward to your thoughts.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Use them verbatim or as a talk track.
Intro Slide
 Hi There, and thank you for taking the time today. We would love to walk you through Harmony Games, show how our platform approach de-risks the hit-making process in puzzle RPG, and share what we are building now. Please jump in with candid feedback, and if this resonates, we would be excited to continue the conversation after this meeting.
Slide: The Company
 I am Leonard, co-founder and CEO of Harmony Games, joined by my co-founders [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Blake and a senior team across product, UA, analytics, Unity, backend, and art. We founded the company in 2023, raised a 3 million dollar seed, and built a lean 17 to 20 person core team operating across the United States, Turkey, Eastern Europe, and South America with low-cost development partners. Our mission is simple and disciplined: rapidly build and test breakthrough mechanics, then scale the winners on a reusable, AI-assisted engine so creativity becomes a defensible advantage rather than a one-off. Our vision is to build the world’s best puzzle RPGs with Turkish execution DNA and global scale.
Slide: Market
 Puzzle RPG is a 1.2 billion dollar mobile category that is ripe for disruption. Eastern titles prove the ceiling while Western match-3 plus RPG clones show fatigue, and the contenders that break out do so with fresh core experiences rather than more of the same. Our thesis is to carve out a Western-first, mechanic-first blue ocean and build the next 100 million dollar puzzle RPG franchise.
Slide: The Harmony Games Engine
 We are not just building games. We are building systems that shorten time to proof and let us reuse success. Version 1.0 of the Harmony Games Engine took roughly 15 months to build. We are now porting those systems into new titles in about four months with production-level quality and full LiveOps integration. The platform spans LiveOps automation, advanced leaderboards, seasonal content, team and social systems, dynamic difficulty, AI-assisted level creation with smart bots, and a flexible 3D puzzle layer with physics and expandable boosters. This is why we can move from concept to soft launch on a single green-light cycle and operate with a small, fast team.
Slide: Engine Demos
 In the meeting, we will show brief clips of the Puzzle Engine and the LiveOps Engine to highlight how content, economy events, and leaderboards are configured without heavy engineering. The important takeaway is that net-new code is minimized while speed and reliability are maximized.
Slide: Pragmatic Marketing AI
 Our user acquisition approach is tool-first, not platform-first. Creative is king in mobile UA, so our pipeline focuses on throughput: concept to first testable video in about two hours, with weekly rotations and hard kills on weak lines. We are already producing playables because networks increasingly favor short interactive ads, and we use best-in-class tools to accelerate hook testing, copy, VO, and assembly without bloating the team.
Slide: Studio Roadmap
 Our cadence is something investors can model. We standardized LiveOps Engine v1.0 and shipped Puzzle Engine v1.0 with an AI co-pilot for level creation. We are iterating toward LiveOps v2.0 for personalization and Puzzle Engine v2.0 for adaptive or auto-generated levels. On this spine, we progress titles in parallel and target a new live beta roughly every four to five months, culminating in Zombie Match 3D global timing on the roadmap.
Slide: Domino Delights
 Domino Delights was our proving ground. We validated the production content pipeline, physics, boosters, effects, events, leaderboards, A/B testing, shop and offers, analytics hygiene, and localization plus build operations. We deliberately de-scoped heavy narrative, UA scale, and long-tail tuning because the goal was to harden the engine, not to over-invest before we had proof.
Slide: LiveOps Event Library
 Retention is a calendar, so we invested early in an expanding LiveOps library. We support single-player events like win-and-collect and unique modes, PvP-style fastest-completion and usage leaderboards, daily and weekly quests, login calendars, season pass and trophy paths, and team systems with GvG underway. These are authorable systems that let us ship frequent, reliable engagement beats from day one.
Slide: Decision Discipline
 Our Turkish DNA is to test, kill, and scale with honesty. Domino Delights creatives and CPI tested well and D1 in the low to mid 40s was encouraging, but D7 settled around the mid teens with a roughly 35 percent D7 to D1 ratio, which capped LTV against CPI outside small budgets. We stopped scaling, shipped the learnings, and pivoted quickly to a better core engagement mechanic while reusing the stack. That discipline unlocked a four-month port to our next title.
Slide: Zombie Match 3D Overview
 Zombie Match 3D is our wedge for Western audiences. The core is rapid-fire 3D “match and slash” where every matched object becomes a weapon, layered with an item arsenal and upgrades for deeper monetization, plus bosses and horde modes for session variety. LiveOps is built in from day one so we can operate like a service, not a demo.
Slide: Zombie Match 3D Progress
 We have a zombie and UI overhaul in progress for beta, and the item upgrade system is built with effects like shockwave, poison, and stun to drive satisfying power curves without harming accessibility. The result is a loop that reads fast and fun while opening room for event-driven depth.
Slide: Zombie LiveOps Status
 LiveOps integration in Zombie Match sits at roughly 60 percent complete with the remaining 40 percent landing on a short horizon. Trophy path, leaderboards, quests, daily gift, and teams are online or in final integration, which means we can move into soft-launch operations with confidence in cadence and tooling.
Slide: Alpha Signals and Near-Term Gates
 Early UK iOS alpha with roughly 300 installs showed D1 around 34 percent, day-zero playtime around 23 minutes, and CPI around 4.5 dollars at minimal polish. Over the next six to eight weeks, we expand content to 500 plus levels, complete the polish and VFX pass, and scale UA to two to three thousand users for stable reads. Our gates are explicit: D1 at least 45 percent, D7 to D1 at least 45 percent, and CPI at or below 3.50 dollars in UK iOS tests. We scale only if the data clears the gates.
Slide: The Raise and Use of Proceeds
 We are raising a 2.5 million dollar bridge that extends runway to 18 months or more. The use of funds is approximately 1.5 million dollars for product and engine and 1.0 million dollars for soft-launch UA. The milestones to unlock the next round before worldwide launch include D1 in the mid to high 40s, D7 in the low to mid 20s, CPI targets by geo and platform, early payer rates, and 60 to 90 day ROAS gates.
Slide: Why Harmony Games
 We believe Harmony Games is an efficient bet on the next breakout in puzzle RPG for three reasons. First, we are platform-first, with modular, AI-assisted systems for puzzle generation, LiveOps, analytics, and UA that are already production-Proven and let us ship a content-ready beta in four to five months once the core game is Proven. Second, we operate with Turkish model discipline: test, kill, and scale, with low burn around 100 thousand dollars per month and clear decision gates that keep CAC and LTV honest, which is uncommon among Western teams. Third, we have a distinct genre wedge with Match and Slash that pairs broad Western appeal and 3D visual punch with RPG monetization depth, positioned to stand out amid look-alikes.
Closing Slide
 Thank you again for your time. We welcome questions on the platform, the roadmap, and the data behind our gates, and we would be glad to dive deeper into the Zombie Match 3D soft-launch plan and the LiveOps v2.0 feature set. Leonard,

Done. The send list is in my Q4 2025 investor update folder as "Q4 update - send list" (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1z8GvB8GBgX-HTCtQTEShXgwTHayNSp1Nevs6PIZdwgw/edit). It's shared with you as an editor and runs as of end of day Sep 30 PT.

Counts by group:
- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $25K, DocuSign completed Sep 26)
- In talks: 7 firms, 0 angels (a16z, NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, GFR Fund, plus HOMA and Brightwater Games Fund, which aren't on the list but had calls on my calendar)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels
- Keep warm: 3 firms, 0 angels (LVP, Hiro Capital, SciPlay)

Total: 25 rows (24 firms, 1 angel).

A few calls to flag for Monday:
- Paul Heydon is off the list. He was going in talks at $50K until he told you on Sep 30 he can't invest this year.
- SciPlay is in Keep warm. D told Robert on Sep 30 that they're passing.
- a16z is still in talks. The speedrun rejection is the program's answer, not their answer on the bridge.
- Build access: the four firms with tester adds (NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, Brightwater) are marked iOS only. Arthur found on Sep 30 that the Play internal track list was never attached, even though the Linear log shows it. The other in-talks firms are marked none.

On the Existing Investor Update card I added checklists for New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm. I also added F/up cards in To Do for everyone in talks or awaiting reply. NCsoft got a comment on the existing "F/up with Anel" card instead of a new one. Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) didn't get cards because they already have meetings on my calendar.

See you Monday.

Fred

The send list is built, the Trello card is done, and I've replied on Leonard's thread. Everything reflects end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific), as his instructions doc asks.

**Send list:** "Q4 update - send list" is a Google Sheet in your Q4 2025 investor update folder, named the way the README asks, and shared with Leonard as an editor. It has one row per firm or angel, with group, amount, build access and a short note on why each one is in that group. There are 25 rows: 24 firms and 1 angel.

| Group | Firms | Angels | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1 | Anton Bernstein, $25K (DocuSign completed Sep 26) |
| In talks | 7 | 0 | a16z, NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, GFR Fund, HOMA, Brightwater Games Fund |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 | Makers Fund, Raine, General Catalyst, BBQ Capital, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo, e2vc, Initial Capital, Treo VC, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital, BITKRAFT |
| Keep warm | 3 | 0 | London Venture Partners, Hiro Capital, SciPlay |

HOMA and Brightwater aren't on the 2025 investor list. They're included because each had a call on your calendar where the bridge was pitched.

**Decisions Leonard may want to go over on Monday:**
- **Paul Heydon is off the list.** He said yes at $50K but never signed, then told Leonard on Sep 30 he can't invest this year.
- **SciPlay moved to Keep warm.** They passed by phone to Robert on Sep 30.
- **a16z stays in talks.** Their rejection was for the speedrun program. Leonard's doc says that doesn't count as their answer on the bridge.
- **Build access:** NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu and Brightwater are marked "iOS only". Arthur's Linear log says they also got Android, but on Sep 30 he found the Play internal-track tester list was never attached. The other in-talks firms are marked "none", since only the public store links reached them.

**Trello:**
- The Existing Investor Update card now has four checklists (New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply, Keep warm), one item per firm or angel.
- I added 18 "F/up with [name]" cards to To Do.
- NCsoft already had a card in To Do ("F/up with Anel after the engine deep dive"), so I commented on it instead of adding another.
- Dentsu and Makers Fund have no follow-up card because they already have meetings on your calendar after Sep 30 (Oct 1 and Oct 8).

**Email:** The reply on Leonard's thread gives the counts per group and the points above. It went to Leonard only, not to Robert and Arthur who were cc'd on his email.

Files are in your Q4 2025 investor update folder:
- Q4 update - send list
